sentences.text: Researchers analyzed brain recordings from participants who made real-time judgments about a soundtrack containing speech and music to determine if basic acoustic features suffice for categorization.
Auditory cortical regions tracked the timing and pitch variations of the audio, employing distinct neural oscillations to process these temporal and spectral dimensions separately.
The resulting neural activity patterns were associated with the ability to predict how a separate group of listeners categorized the sounds as either speech or music.
Specifically, the left hemisphere demonstrated superior tracking of speech-related features, whereas the right hemisphere was more effective at tracking music-related features.
These findings suggest that the brain's fundamental coding of sound features is sufficient to distinguish speech from music without requiring more complex abstract processing.
